headline: Sterling is about 1.3303 dollars this morning, edging down from 1.3312 last night as the dollar held near a two week high against the pound and the euro. Today brings the UK Budget at 16:30 Dubai and the Fed's decision at 22:00 Dubai, where a hold is expected but markets price about an 84% chance of a rise in December.

drivers.title: Fed rate expectations
drivers.text: The Fed's range is 3.75% to 4% and its decision is due today, Wednesday 28 October, at 22:00 Dubai, with Chair Kevin Warsh speaking at 22:30 Dubai. CME FedWatch implied a 92.8% chance of a hold today and an 84.4% chance of a rise in December, FXStreet reported early on 28 October. A statement or press conference that leans towards a December rise would lift the dollar.

drivers.title: Bond yields and the dollar
drivers.text: Global bond yields have been rising, which FXStreet cited on 28 October as a weight on the pound, and the US ten year yield was about 4.98% on the evening of Monday 26 October. The dollar has had three days of gains to a near two week high. Higher US yields make the dollar more rewarding to hold, and lower ones the reverse.

drivers.title: Oil and the Gulf
drivers.text: Brent fell about 1% to around $114.80 (about £86.30) early on Tuesday 27 October, a second day of falls, as Saudi, Turkish and Pakistani officials met Iran in Tehran to discuss easing the conflict, while Houthi attacks on Saudi targets kept the market cautious. President Trump has said he will soon choose between a deal with Iran and resuming strikes. Dearer oil and Gulf tension tend to lift the dollar, and easing tension the reverse.

drivers.title: The UK side
drivers.text: Bank Rate is 3.75% and on 23 October money markets priced at least three quarter point rises by April 2027, the first possibly on 5 November, after September inflation of 3.5%. Bank of England policymaker Megan Greene said in remarks reported on 28 October that wage growth has stopped slowing at a level above what fits 2% inflation, which FXStreet read as leaning towards higher rates. The Chancellor, John Healey, presents his first Budget today at 16:30 Dubai; Scotiabank expects a Budget that keeps borrowing credible to leave the pound little changed at worst, while more borrowing than expected could weigh on it.

drivers.title: Europe and the wider mood
drivers.text: EUR/USD held just below 1.1150 (about £0.84) early on Wednesday, and the European Central Bank meets on Thursday 29 October. Results from Alphabet, Microsoft and Amazon this week could shape confidence in spending on artificial intelligence. A firmer euro tends to go with a softer dollar, while a nervous mood in markets tends to steady it.

lower: A Fed statement or press conference today that leans towards a December rise, which would lift US yields and the dollar.
A Budget today that unsettles the gilt market with more borrowing than expected, which would weigh on the pound.
Renewed US strikes on Iran or further Houthi attacks pushing oil back up from about $115 (about £86.30), which would tend to lift the dollar.
US core inflation (PCE) on Thursday above the 0.3% expected, or growth above the 3.2% forecast, which would keep a December Fed rise in view and support the dollar.
higher: A Fed that plays down a December rise today, which would lower US yields and weaken the dollar.
A Budget that reassures the gilt market, which would remove a weight on the pound while the case for a Bank of England rise on 5 November stands.
Progress in the mediation with Iran or a deal with the US, which would bring oil down, ease US inflation worries and weaken the dollar.
Softer US core inflation or growth on Thursday than forecast, which would make a December Fed rise less certain.
watch: Today brings the UK Budget at 16:30 Dubai, then the Fed's decision at 22:00 Dubai, where a hold is expected, and Chair Warsh's press conference at 22:30 Dubai. A Budget that calms the gilt market, and a Fed that plays down a December rise, would both help someone selling pounds for dirhams; US growth (3.2% forecast) and core inflation (PCE, 0.3% forecast) follow at 16:30 Dubai on Thursday, where lower figures would help.

feed.title: The dollar has stayed firm overnight ahead of the Budget and the Fed
feed.text: GBP/USD drifted from 1.3312 at 20:40 Dubai last night to a low of 1.3301 at 05:49 Dubai and was near 1.3303 at 07:40 Dubai, while EUR/USD eased by a similar share, from 1.1131 to 1.1126, and the pound did not move against the euro, so this was the dollar holding near a two week high rather than news about the pound. FXStreet reports no single news item behind it, pointing to caution before the UK Budget at 16:30 Dubai and the Fed's decision at 22:00 Dubai, and to rising bond yields around the world, which tend to support the dollar.

feed.title: Sterling has slipped on the eve of the Budget
feed.text: GBP/USD eased from 1.3333 at 18:34 Dubai to a low of 1.3306 at 20:20 Dubai and was near 1.3312 at 20:40 Dubai, while EUR/USD fell only slightly, from 1.1150 to 1.1143, and the pound lost a little against the euro too, so this leg was mostly the pound softening rather than the dollar firming. FXStreet describes a third day of losses for sterling as traders wait for the UK Budget at 16:30 Dubai on Wednesday and the Fed's decision that evening; no report found names a single news item behind this afternoon's dip.

feed.title: US consumer confidence has jumped, with little lasting effect on sterling
feed.text: The Conference Board's index rose to 91.7 in October against 81.2 expected, up from a revised 84.2 in September, helped by lower petrol prices. A stronger US consumer usually firms the dollar by keeping a December Fed rise in view, and GBP/USD did dip from 1.3320 to 1.3316 in the first minute, but it then rose to 1.3333 by 18:10 Dubai and settled near 1.3329, so the surprise did not move the rate for long ahead of Wednesday's Fed decision.

feed.title: The dollar has eased back from this morning's high
feed.text: GBP/USD has climbed from a one week low of 1.3305 at 13:40 Dubai to 1.3327 by 16:07 Dubai, while EUR/USD rose by a similar share, from 1.1138 to 1.1150, and the pound barely moved against the euro, so this is the dollar giving back part of the gains it made this morning ahead of the Fed's meeting. No report found names a cause; the last leg, from 1.3317 to 1.3327, came in the minutes after New York desks opened at 16:00 Dubai.

feed.title: The dollar has kept firming through the London morning
feed.text: GBP/USD eased from 1.3325 at 11:30 Dubai to 1.3322 at 13:05 Dubai, then slid to a one week low of 1.3306 by 13:35 Dubai, while EUR/USD fell by a similar share, from 1.1164 to 1.1137, so this was the dollar gaining against both rather than the pound weakening. FXStreet puts it down to steady dollar buying ahead of the Fed's two day meeting, which starts today, and names no single news item; markets expect a hold on Wednesday but a rise in December, and expected US rises tend to strengthen the dollar and lower the number of dirhams per pound.

feed.title: The dollar has firmed overnight, taking sterling to about 1.3326
feed.text: GBP/USD eased from 1.3355 at 22:07 Dubai to about 1.3340 by midnight, held there through Asian trading, then slipped to a low of 1.3315 by 11:00 Dubai, while EUR/USD fell by a similar share, from 1.1190 to 1.1163, and the pound barely moved against the euro, so this was the dollar firming rather than news about the pound. No report found names a single cause; traders are positioning before the UK Budget at 16:30 Dubai on Wednesday and the Fed's decision at 22:00 Dubai the same evening.

feed.title: The dollar firmed this afternoon as oil rose, then eased back
feed.text: GBP/USD fell from 1.3378 before London opened to about 1.3340 by 13:30 Dubai, as the pound weakened against the euro ahead of Wednesday's Budget, then dipped to 1.3327 at about 18:00 Dubai as the dollar firmed against everything, with EUR/USD down from 1.1213 to 1.1179. Brent rose to about $117 (about £87.60) a barrel and analysts pointed to a third US aircraft carrier group in the Gulf, and dearer oil and Gulf tension tend to lift the dollar, while the pound held up better against the euro in the afternoon. By 22:00 Dubai both had recovered, with GBP/USD back near 1.3354 and the US ten year yield about 4.98%, so the day has been a round trip inside about 0.4%.

feed.title: Sterling has slipped since London opened
feed.text: GBP/USD fell from 1.3373 at the London opening at 11:00 Dubai to 1.3343 by 12:40 Dubai, with roughly half the fall from a firmer dollar (EUR/USD eased from 1.1217 to 1.1206) and half from a softer pound (EUR/GBP rose from 0.8388 to 0.8396). No report found names a cause; the morning's coverage notes only that sterling was 0.14% lower at 1.3358 dollars while oil eased and investors waited for Wednesday's Budget. Cheaper oil would usually weaken the dollar, so the oil price does not explain this morning's firmer dollar.

feed.title: The pound has slipped against the euro ahead of Wednesday's Budget
feed.text: The dollar has eased about 0.2% against the euro since Friday's close, but the pound has lost a similar share against the euro, with EUR/GBP up from 0.8371 to 0.8390, so GBP/USD is little changed and slipped from 1.3380 at 07:30 Dubai to 1.3370 by 09:50 Dubai. No report names a cause this morning, but investors are cautious before the Budget at 16:30 Dubai on Wednesday, after long-dated gilt yields traded above 6% this month for the first time since 1998, and analysts see the pound's risks into the Budget as tilted to the downside. At least three Bank of England rises by April 2027 are already priced, so the rate outlook on its own is not lifting the pound further.

feed.title: The dollar has eased as oil slips on Qatari mediation
feed.text: Brent fell 1.6% to $114.88 (about £85.90) a barrel in early Asian trade on Monday after reports that Qatari mediators were in Tehran on Sunday, working with the US to ease tensions, and the US ten year yield eased to 4.97%, Reuters reported. Cheaper oil and lower US yields tend to weaken the dollar, and EUR/USD rose from 1.1199 to 1.1222 over the same hours, so this was the dollar easing rather than the pound gaining. GBP/USD held near 1.3366 after the reopening at 01:00 Dubai, then rose from 1.3362 at 03:20 Dubai to 1.3378 by 04:00 Dubai and was near 1.3380 at 07:30 Dubai.

feed.title: Trump says it is decision time on Iran
feed.text: In a Fox News interview on Sunday, President Trump said he must choose between a deal with Iran and resuming strikes, suggested strikes could follow the 3 November midterms, and said there would be no strike that day. Gulf tension tends to lift the dollar, but the weekend price took it calmly: Kraken's GBP/USD eased from 1.3375 at Friday's close and stayed mostly between 1.3360 and 1.3376 through Sunday.

feed.title: The dollar has firmed as oil tops $116
feed.text: Brent rose about 2.6% to $116.13 (about £86.90) a barrel on Friday, its highest since 30 April, as traders priced in renewed US strikes on Iran and Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia went on; the US ten year yield edged back up to about 4.99%. Dearer oil and Gulf tension tend to lift the dollar, and EUR/USD fell from 1.1204 to 1.1193 over the same hours, so this was mainly the dollar firming, with the pound also a touch softer against the euro. GBP/USD eased from 1.3385 at 18:55 Dubai to 1.3360 by 21:20 Dubai and was near 1.3362 at 21:35 Dubai; no single headline marks the start of the slide.

feed.title: US business surveys were mixed, with prices rising fast
feed.text: The flash October surveys put US manufacturing at 56.0 against 55.5 expected and services at 57.9 against 58.0, with the composite down to 57.6 from 58.4; firms raised selling prices at the sharpest rate since August 2022. Faster price rises add to the case for a December Fed rise, which tends to lift the dollar. GBP/USD dipped from 1.3373 just before 17:45 Dubai to 1.3366 within four minutes, then recovered to 1.3377 by 17:53 Dubai.

feed.title: US consumer mood was revised up, with inflation worries steady
feed.text: The University of Michigan's final October sentiment reading was 48.0 against 46.3 expected from the first estimate, little changed on September's 48.1, while consumers' year ahead inflation expectation held at 4.7% and the long run measure rose to 3.5%. A firmer reading and rising inflation expectations lean slightly towards a stronger dollar, but the reaction was small: GBP/USD moved from 1.3376 to 1.3377 at 18:01 Dubai, slipped to 1.3372 by 18:05 Dubai and was back near 1.3377 by 18:38 Dubai.

feed.title: The dollar has firmed as oil climbs on attacks on Saudi Arabia
feed.text: Brent rose above $114 (about £85.30) a barrel on Friday morning, up more than 1% and at its highest in over five months, after Yemen's Houthis claimed strikes on Saudi targets including the Yanbu refinery, which caught fire. Dearer oil and Gulf tension tend to lift the dollar, and the dollar index rose about 0.2% on the day. GBP/USD eased from 1.3382 at 14:15 Dubai to 1.3370 by 15:35 Dubai while EUR/USD fell by a similar share and the pound held steady against the euro, so this was the dollar firming; no report ties the late morning dip to a single headline.

feed.title: UK business surveys have beaten forecasts
feed.text: The flash October surveys showed UK services at 53.1 against 51.8 expected and manufacturing at 52.8 against about 51.8, both up on September. Firmer UK activity supports the case for a Bank of England rise on 5 November, and the pound gained on the euro, while GBP/USD rose from 1.3380 to 1.3385 within a minute, then slipped to 1.3374 by 08:36 UTC as the dollar firmed across the board, a move no source has yet explained.

feed.title: UK shoppers spent less than expected in September
feed.text: Retail sales volumes fell 0.4% in September against a forecast fall of 0.1%, and fell 0.7% without fuel, though August was revised up to a 0.7% rise; the ONS put the drop down to warm weather hitting winter clothing and a dip in supermarket sales. Weaker spending trims slightly the case for a Bank of England rise on 5 November, which tends to weigh on the pound. The reaction was small: GBP/USD slipped from 1.3388 just before 10:00 Dubai to 1.3384 within a minute, held near 1.3386 for twenty minutes, then recovered to 1.3392.

feed.title: Sterling has eased slightly overnight as the dollar steadied
feed.text: GBP/USD drifted from 1.3401 at 05:35 Dubai to 1.3392 by 06:00 Dubai and was near 1.3394 at 07:35 Dubai, while EUR/USD fell by the same 0.07%, from 1.1220 to 1.1211, so this was the dollar firming rather than the pound weakening. No report explains the move; it came in quiet Asian trading with Brent steady near $113.7 (about £84.90) and the US ten year yield still below 5% at about 4.97%.

feed.title: The dollar has weakened as US bond yields fell sharply
feed.text: US government bond yields had their biggest one day fall in more than two years as investors left technology shares for bonds after disappointing results from Meta and Tesla: the ten year yield was down 11 basis points to 5.02% by 19:13 Dubai and below 5% by 20:55 Dubai, Yahoo Finance reported. Lower US yields make the dollar less rewarding to hold, so more dirhams per pound; EUR/USD rose by a similar margin while the pound hardly moved against the euro, so this was the dollar softening. GBP/USD rose from 1.3369 at 19:25 Dubai to 1.3407 by 21:15 Dubai and was near 1.3403 at 22:35 Dubai.

feed.title: Fewer Americans claimed jobless benefits last week
feed.text: New claims for unemployment benefits fell to 194,000 in the week to 17 October, against 200,000 expected, and the week before was revised up to 200,000. Fewer claims point to a US job market that is still firm, which supports the dollar, but the effect was small: GBP/USD dipped from 1.3373 to 1.3368 within a minute of the release, then recovered to about 1.3372 by 12:32 UTC.

feed.title: The dollar has firmed on reports of planned strikes on Iran
feed.text: GBP/USD fell from 1.3382 at 14:54 Dubai to 1.3361 by 15:09 Dubai and was near 1.3366 at 15:36 Dubai, while EUR/USD fell by a similar margin and the pound hardly moved against the euro, so this was the dollar strengthening. No report ties a piece of news to that quarter hour, but just before it CNBC reported a New York Times account that the US and Israeli militaries have drawn up plans for a short but intensive operation against Iran after next month's midterm elections, with Brent near $112 (about £84). Gulf tension and dearer oil tend to lift the dollar, so fewer dirhams per pound.

feed.title: Sterling has slipped as the dollar firmed in a nervous market
feed.text: GBP/USD fell from 1.3407 at 13:42 Dubai to 1.3379 by 14:09 Dubai and was near 1.3382 at 14:36 Dubai. EUR/USD fell by about 0.12% over the same half hour while the pound eased only slightly against the euro, so this was mostly the dollar strengthening. No report ties a piece of news to that half hour, but the mood is nervous: Iranian state television said seven tankers were damaged overnight in the Strait of Hormuz, Brent rose about 3% to near $112 (about £84), European shares fell by around 1%, and a nervous market with dearer oil tends to lift the dollar, so fewer dirhams per pound.

feed.title: The dollar has slipped again around midday
feed.text: GBP/USD fell to 1.3397 at 12:08 Dubai, then climbed to 1.3418 by 12:26 Dubai before settling near 1.3408 at 12:38 Dubai. EUR/USD rose from 1.1229 to 1.1242 over the same quarter hour while the euro hardly moved against the pound, so this was the dollar softening rather than the pound rising. No report found explains the move: Trading Economics describes the dollar index as steady near 101.7 on Thursday, with a Fed hold expected next week, and oil has risen rather than fallen this morning.

feed.title: Oil has climbed after a drone strike on a Saudi oil field
feed.text: Brent rose about 1.7% to near $110.70 (about £82.60) a barrel on Thursday morning, Trading Economics reported, after debris from a drone shot down near Aramco's Shaybah field killed two workers and the US ordered non-emergency embassy staff out of Saudi Arabia. Dearer oil and Gulf tension tend to lift the dollar, yet sterling held its ground overnight: GBP/USD dipped from 1.3400 at 22:00 Dubai on Wednesday to 1.3381 by 23:00 Dubai, recovered to about 1.3394, and was near 1.3383 at 06:00 Dubai.
